description:
Goal
Write characterization tests that describe the desired transport authority before changing the model. These tests should observe the behavior we must preserve and the old structures we intend to remove.

Signal
Tests cover single-lane returns, ignored inputs/results, tuple-field returns/resumes, direct callable returns/resumes, escaped callable publication through BoundaryId, opaque callable boundaries, closure captures, backend interpreter parity, and native JIT delivery. Existing tests that assert RuntimeValueLayout, DeliveredShape, NativeDemandAbi, or local repr derivation as authority are marked for rewrite to interned spine/fact assertions.

Worked-example contract
Pin the paper model from outline.md in executable form: a tuple-field return containing a direct callable is transported without tuple or heap closure allocation; the producer return and consumer resume use the same shape; direct callable invocation reads CallableId target/capture facts; an escaped callable publishes a BoundaryId contract; codegen repr is asserted as a seam fact, not shape.

Strategy
Use the current fixtures and telemetry capture harnesses. Add tests only where a behavior is not already pinned. Do not add compatibility helpers. The tests should state intent: one settled ShapeId graph plus fact-table projections keyed by TransportPosition, LaneId, CallableId, BoundaryId, and codegen seam.

Removal target identified
RuntimeValueLayout assertions in drive/artifact tests, DeliveredShape/NativeDemandAbi assertions in native codegen tests, local ArgRepr-from-type expectations, boundary-return projection expectations, and any stale ValueRef expectations at exact internal transport seams.

Checks
cargo test for the targeted compiler2 transport tests; rg inventory shows old transport-type assertions are either removed or rewritten to spine/fact assertions.
title: Transport spine: pin ShapeId/LaneId/BoundaryId contracts before the cutover
